protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3; refute not confirm; two severable owner-recording entries under adopted D-054 / D-057
summary: The subject held frozen start to end. This is the first exercise of adopted D-057's mechanics, and almost all of it lands: both entries are severable with their own dependencies, authority pins, subject, owner role, rider statement and reversibility, and every one of the four cited commits resolves to the right decision while all seven cited digests match live bytes. D-054 and D-057 are both still ADOPTED and unsuperseded, which is D-057's own precondition. One SHOULD-FIX blocks consent. D-057's pin list, incorporated from its adopted turn-3 subject, requires 'both verdict paths and sha256s'; these entries supply the four verdict sha256s in the measured-inputs table under labels rather than paths, and the string count for verdict paths in the draft is zero. The disposition is likewise given as a bare filename rather than a path. Nothing is unidentifiable — I resolved every digest — but the first exercise of a required-pin rule should match the rule it exercises.

objections.location: Measured inputs table and both entries' Authority pins / Subject blocks
objections.claim: The D-057 pin list requires verdict paths as well as digests, and the entries supply digests only. The disposition is given as a filename rather than a path on the same reasoning.
evidence: Adopted D-057 requires later owner-recording entries to 'satisfy the preconditions and pins in the adopted turn-3 subject', and that subject's clause 3 reads: 'file-08 owner role; disposition path and sha256; both verdict paths and sha256s; preview scope; Route A remainder; coordinator-recording decision ID and commit; every operative rider or binding advisory that recording adopted.'

The four verdicts appear only in the measured-inputs table, keyed by the labels 'DR-002 Claude 2 v2', 'DR-002 Codex v2', 'DR-004 Claude 2 v2' and 'DR-004 Codex v2', each with a sha256 and 'ACCEPT 0/0'. I counted occurrences of the verdict path strings in the draft: zero.

The disposition appears as 'route-b.DR-002.preview-disposition.v2.json' and 'route-b.DR-004.preview-disposition.v2.json' — filenames, two occurrences — with zero full paths under docs/coop/artifacts/. By contrast the D-054 pin is done correctly, giving the full path 'docs/coop/artifacts/coordinator-decisions.D-054.user-amendment.md' with its sha256 and commit, which shows the entry knows the required form and applies it unevenly.
objections.whyOnlyShouldFix: Nothing is unidentifiable. A sha256 fixes bytes uniquely, and I resolved all four verdict digests and both disposition digests to the correct files and confirmed each against live bytes without ambiguity. The authority chain is therefore verifiable today, which is why this is not a blocker on the recording's substance.
objections.whyItStillBlocksConsent: D-057 is a mechanics entry whose sole function is to fix the required pins, and this is the first exercise of it. A pin list is a closed checklist; supplying six of seven elements in the stated form and one in a weaker form sets the precedent every later owner recording will copy. The cost of compliance is four path strings.
objections.remedy: Give the four verdict paths beside their sha256s, and the two disposition paths in full, in the same form the D-054 pin already uses.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 81b67b5b41edcd0cf5f9db94d11519ad456104e20f5ae43e6444138b9522db1e, measured three times at start and again at end, all equal to the dispatched frozen digest. The dispatch made motion an OBJECT condition and it does not arise.
D-057's live-adoption precondition holds, which I checked at the register rather than assuming: D-054 and D-057 are both present, both ADOPTED, and neither carries OVERTURNED or SUPERSEDED.

All four cited commits resolve to the correct decisions: 29670ed is 'D-054: user amendment for preview-scope owner recording', 33597e8 is 'D-057: mechanics for preview-scope owner recording', aa75926 is 'D-047/D-048: select Route B for DR-002 and DR-004 preview', and 88764fa is 'D-049/D-050: record accepted Route B drafts for DR-002 and DR-004'. The shared commits for the D-047/D-048 pair and the D-049/D-050 pair are correct rather than a copy error — those entries were adopted together.
All nine cited digests match live bytes: the D-054 user amendment, both dispositions, all four verdicts, COORD and file 08.

The verdict characterizations are exact for my half. Both entries recite 'ACCEPT 0/0' for the Claude 2 v2 verdicts, and I returned ACCEPT with 0 blockers and 0 advisories on both DR-002 and DR-004 v2.

The attack 'silent SATISFIED' fails. The header carries '**Does not** mark SATISFIED', each entry's clause 3 states 'Does not mark DR-002 SATISFIED' and 'Does not mark DR-004 SATISFIED', and each Readiness effect line states 'Zero SATISFIED.'

The attack 'treats ACCEPT as SATISFIED' fails and the entries keep the distinction the corpus has been careful about: they record the disposition as owner-recorded, state the condition-1 effect as 'may discharge … within architecture-preview scope only', and separately refuse SATISFIED.

The attack 'discharges AC-1/AC-3/AC-4 or the Phase-1A packet' fails. D-058 clause 3 states 'AC-1, AC-3, and AC-4 stay owed on Route A'; D-059 clause 3 states 'The eight-bullet Phase-1A packet stays owed on Route A. section31 v4 stays the binding instrument, not the packet.' Both match what I verified when reviewing those dispositions.

The attack 'unsverable bundle' fails at three levels: the header states 'Adopting or overturning one does not adopt or overturn the other'; each entry carries its own Severable line naming the sibling; and each has its own Dependencies, Authority pins, Subject, Owner role, Decision, Readiness effect and Reversibility with distinct overturn commits C-D058 and C-D059.

The dependency declaration D-057 requires is present in both, in the required form: 'Dependencies (D-057 clause 3): D-054, D-057, and D-047' — or D-048 — followed by 'Revocation or overturn requires this owner's supersession and reconciliation of dependent MF-6 notes.'

The rider requirement is satisfied and correctly reasoned rather than left blank: 'Operative riders: none. D-049 recorded ACCEPT 0/0 with no rider. No ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES advisories to classify.' That is right — both v2 dispositions were ACCEPT at 0 advisories, so there is nothing to carry, unlike DR-005 where D-039's RB-DR005-V2-A1 would have to travel.

The attacks 'file 08 edited' and 'condition 5 / docs/v2/implementation' fail: each entry's clause 4 states 'Does not edit file 08 (MF-6). A later cell note is a separate act', each clause 3 states 'Conditions 2–5 remain. Condition 5 remains the only implementation authorization', the header refuses to authorize docs/v2/implementation/, file 08 measures unchanged, and git reports zero modified tracked files.
The owner roles match file 08: 'Evidence authority + V1 coordinator' for DR-002 and 'Evidence/retention authority' for DR-004, which are the owner cells I extracted when reviewing D-049 and D-050.

Reversibility is the correct compound form for an act with dependents and is properly severed: 'Compound. Overturn: C-D058, plus reconciliation of any later MF-6 note. Does not overturn D-047, D-049, D-054, or D-057.'
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex review of this subject. Not read; the file is confirmed absent at review time.

The Codex verdicts on the two v2 dispositions, whose digests I verified but whose contents I have not read. Both entries recite them as ACCEPT 0/0; if either characterization is wrong, D-057's dual-ACCEPT precondition fails and nothing in my review would detect it.

Whether these entries have since been superseded. While reviewing I observed a later dispatch covering D-059 through D-063, which suggests this two-entry draft may have been reorganized; that is outside this subject and I have graded only the frozen bytes I was given.

Whether the preview-scope condition-1 discharge these entries effect is substantively correct. That turns on D-054's authority, which is the user amendment I objected to in its coordinator-composed form and which is now adopted; this entry correctly exercises it rather than re-granting.
The merits of the two v2 dispositions beyond my separate ACCEPT reviews of each, whose stated limits I carry forward.

environment.gitHeadSubject: D-057: mechanics for preview-scope owner recording
environment.note: The subject is an untracked working-tree file and held at the dispatched frozen digest throughout.
environment.measurementTool: shasum -a 256 of the subject three times at start and again at end; git log --format=%s on each of the four cited commits; digest verification of all nine cited inputs against live bytes; awk extraction of adopted D-057's decision text and of adopted D-054/D-057 status for the live-adoption precondition; string counts for verdict paths, disposition filenames and full artifact paths in the draft; git status across file 08 and COORD

nonConsentNote: I do not CONSENT, on one SHOULD-FIX, and the entries are otherwise well built — this is the first owner recording under D-054/D-057 and it gets the hard parts right: severability, live-adoption preconditions, correct commits, correct owner roles, an explicit and correctly reasoned 'no riders' statement, and a compound reversibility that does not reach back into the authorities it depends on. My objection is that D-057's pin list asks for 'both verdict paths and sha256s' and these entries give the sha256s under labels, with zero verdict paths in the file. Nothing is unidentifiable and I resolved every digest myself, which is why it is not a blocker. But a mechanics rule exists to be matched exactly, this is its first exercise, and the fix is four strings.
